VeriTrust is enforcing a new default rate limit of **50 verification requests per second per tenant** starting from November 1, 2026. Partners with negotiated plans retain their agreed limits, but any requests exceeding these limits will receive an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header [S1].

This change impacts Helio Systems because our verification client previously had no retry with backoff and a 5-second timeout, which led to failures when requests were queued beyond the old limits [S3]. To address this, we have already increased the timeout to 15 seconds, added exponential backoff with 3 retries, and agreed on a higher rate limit with VeriTrust [S2]. However, the new default limit may still require us to verify that our client respects the 50 requests per second limit to avoid further timeouts or failures.

The synchronous integration design means that provisioning waits for the verification result, so rate limiting directly affects onboarding latency and success [S5][S6].
